questions.title: Wilcoxon rank-sum statistic under the null (placeholder)
questions.text: Let $X_1,\dots,X_m$ and $Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ be independent samples from the same continuous distribution (the null hypothesis), and put $N=m+n$. Let $R_1,\dots,R_m$ be the ranks of the $X_i$ in the pooled sample, so that the Wilcoxon rank-sum statistic is $W=\sum_{i=1}^m R_i$. Under the null, $(R_1,\dots,R_m)$ is a simple random sample drawn without replacement from $\{1,\dots,N\}$.

markingScheme.step: Each $R_i$ is uniform on $\{1,\dots,N\}$ by exchangeability under the null

parts.modelAnswer:
Under the null the pooled observations are exchangeable and, being continuous, have no ties, so each $R_i$ is uniformly distributed on $\{1,\dots,N\}$. Hence
$$\E[R_i]=\frac1N\sum_{k=1}^N k=\frac{N+1}2 ,$$
and by linearity $\E[W]=\sum_{i=1}^m\E[R_i]=\dfrac{m(N+1)}2$. $\blacksquare$

markingScheme.step: $\Var(R_1)=\frac{N^2-1}{12}$ from the variance of the discrete uniform distribution on $\{1,\dots,N\}$
Uses $\sum_{k=1}^N R_k=N(N+1)/2$ (all ranks) being constant, so its variance is $0$, to find $\Cov(R_i,R_j)=-\frac{N+1}{12}$

parts.modelAnswer:
For the discrete uniform distribution on $\{1,\dots,N\}$, $\Var(R_1)=(N^2-1)/12$. By symmetry all pairs have the same covariance $c$. Summing over all $N$ ranks gives a constant, so
$$0=\Var\Big(\sum_{k=1}^N R_k\Big)=N\cdot\frac{N^2-1}{12}+N(N-1)\,c\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c=-\frac{N+1}{12}.$$
Therefore
\begin{align}
\Var(W)&=m\,\frac{N^2-1}{12}+m(m-1)\Big(-\frac{N+1}{12}\Big)=\frac{m(N+1)}{12}\big[(N-1)-(m-1)\big]\\
&=\frac{m(N+1)(N-m)}{12}=\frac{mn(N+1)}{12}. \qquad\blacksquare
\end{align}

parts.text: With $m=5$, $n=6$ and an observed $W=40$, compute $\E[W]$, $\Var(W)$ and the standardised statistic $z=(W-\E[W])/\sqrt{\Var(W)}$ (no continuity correction).
